name: Dull Magenta Purple
lede: Dull Magenta Purple is a muted reddish purple plotted on Ridgway's 1912 color atlas and later absorbed into the ISCC-NBS dictionary as a moderate reddish purple.

sections.title: A plate in Ridgway's atlas
sections.body:
Robert Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue on plate XXVI at hue 67′, tone i, a systematic grid reference rather than a descriptive name [1]. The scan of that aged printed plate is only an approximation of the original ink [1]. The ISCC-NBS circular of 1955 folds the same region into block 237, where it calls the family strong reddish purple, Munsell notation 3.0RP 4.2/8.2 [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[magenta-haze]], [[twilight-lavender]], [[light-plum]] and [[razzmic-berry]], at 2.6, 3, 4.1 and 4.9 ΔE [2]. The name sits between [[purple]] and [[magenta]], closer to the dusty, grayed end of that range than to [[fandango]], a brighter purple from the same block [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This exact hue is rare in our archive of 23,781 paintings: a match within six units covers at least five percent of the canvas in only 2 of them, as photographed [4]. Both appear after 1850, one a devotional figure painting and one Paul Signac's *Women by the Well* from 1892 [4]. The color splits evenly between mid-tones and shadow in those two paintings, with no clear pattern beyond that small count [4]. A sample this small supports no broader claim about painters or periods [4].
